issues.description: Field Farm.animals has conflicting types across the materials. In the UML fragment in problem_statement.md (line 17) the attribute is declared as List<Animal>. In the textual Part 3 instructions in problem_statement.md (lines 108-109) the text explicitly requires a Set implemented with a HashSet and states uniqueness of animals. The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, lines 9-13) implements the field as a List<Animal> backed by an ArrayList. This mismatch (UML: List vs. text: Set vs. solution: List/ArrayList) leaves students unsure whether to implement Farm.animals as a List or a Set and whether uniqueness/HashSet semantics are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical collection type and apply it consistently. Preferred fix (align with textual intent of uniqueness): change the UML and the solution/template to use Set<Animal> for Farm.animals and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor; update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal> and update any code that depends on List-specific behavior. Alternative fix (if uniqueness is not intended): change the Part 3 textual instructions to require a List (remove HashSet/unique-animal wording) so the UML, template, and solution consistently use List/ArrayList. Apply the chosen change to problem_statement.md (both UML and textual part), the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, and the reference solution to remove the contradiction.
